heroHeadline: AFP Calls China's Pressure Across Batanes, Scarborough Shoal 'Synchronized' as Drilling-Capable Survey Vessel Returns to Guangdong After 30 Days
heroSubtitle: AFP spokesperson Rear Admiral (ret.) Roy Vincent Trinidad said on September 8, 2026 that Chinese activity across three fronts — a mainland Chinese academic claim that Batanes belongs to China as an extension of Taiwan, pressure at Bajo de Masinloc (Scarborough Shoal), and at Ayungin (Second Thomas) Shoal — forms a 'synchronized, persistent' campaign of foreign malign influence, not isolated incidents. He confirmed Chinese fighter jets had put a Philippine patrol aircraft under weapons crosshairs near Scarborough Shoal on September 2. Separately, the PCG confirmed on September 11 that the drilling-capable Chinese survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi Shihao had returned to Guangdong Province after spending 30 days in the Philippine EEZ (Aug 10–Sep 9), 28 of them off Scarborough Shoal, without a DFA permit — a voyage PCG spokesman Jay Tarriela and the Chinese Embassy's Guo Wei publicly disputed as legal or illegal. The developments follow the September 8 incident in which a Chinese embassy note was handed to Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. onstage at the Seoul Defense Dialogue, which he read aloud and called 'coercion, bullying and aggression'; Beijing told him to 'stop the theatrics' the next day.
